zh: 胡雪岩全传——灯火楼台
en: Hu Xueyan: Towers of Light

zh: 光绪七年三月初七，胡雪岩终于践约抵达北京。同行的有两个洋人，一个是在华经商多年，泰来洋行的经理，德国人福克，一个是英商汇丰银行的代表凯密伦。由于这年天气格外冷，天津海口尚未解冻，所以胡雪岩是从陆路来的，浩浩荡荡十几辆车，一进右安门，直投前门外草厂十条胡同阜康福钱庄。为了接待东家，“大伙”汪惟贤十天以前就预备好了，车队一到，胡雪岩与他的客人，还有古应春与办笔墨的杨师爷，被接入客厅，特为挑出来的四名伶俐的学徒，倒脸水倒茶，忙个不停。胡雪岩是汪惟贤亲自照料，一面伺候，一面问讯旅况。
en: On the seventh day of the third lunar month in the seventh year of Guangxu, Hu Xueyan at last fulfilled his promise and arrived in Beijing. Two foreigners accompanied him: Focke, a German who had traded in China for many years and managed the Tailai Trading House, and Cameron, a representative of the British-owned Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. The weather had been exceptionally cold that year, and the harbour at Tianjin was still frozen, so Hu had travelled overland. His imposing procession of more than ten carriages entered You’an Gate and made straight for Fukangfu Bank in Caochang Shitiao Hutong outside Qianmen. Wang Weixian, the head manager, had begun preparing for his employer’s arrival ten days earlier. As soon as the carriages stopped, Hu and his guests, together with Gu Yingchun and Secretary Yang, who handled his correspondence, were ushered into the reception room. Four bright apprentices, specially chosen for the occasion, hurried about bringing water for washing and pouring tea. Wang attended to Hu himself, seeing to his needs while asking about the journey.

zh: 乱过一阵，坐定下来，胡雪岩贴身小斯之一的保福，捧着金水烟袋来为胡雪岩装烟，同时悄声说道：“张姨太已经打发丫头来催请了。”“现在哪里有工夫？”话中似嫌张姨娘不懂事。保福不作声，只望着屏风后面一个十六七岁的丫头摇一摇手，表示胡雪岩还不能进去。由南到北，通都大邑中，有阜康钱庄，就有胡雪岩的一处“行馆”，大多有女主人，住在阜康福后进的张姨娘，不甚得宠，所以胡雪岩有这种语气。
en: When the bustle had subsided and they were seated, Baofu, one of Hu’s personal attendants, brought his gold water pipe and filled it for him. “Madam Zhang has already sent her maid to ask you to come in,” he murmured. “How can I possibly find time now?” Hu’s tone suggested that Madam Zhang ought to know better. Baofu said nothing. He merely waved a hand at a maid of sixteen or seventeen standing behind the screen, indicating that Hu could not come in yet. From south to north, in the great cities where Fukang had branches, Hu also maintained residences, most of them with a woman in charge. Madam Zhang, the concubine who occupied the rear quarters of Fukangfu, was not a particular favourite; hence his tone.

zh: “大先生，”汪惟贤来请示：“是用中菜，还是大菜。”紧接着又表功：“恐怕两位外国客人吃不来中菜，特为跟文大人借了个做大菜的厨子，都预备好了。”所谓“文大人”指的是刑部尚书文煜，他是正蓝旗的满洲人，同治七年出任福州将军。清兵入关，在冲要之地没有驻防的将军坐镇，其中福州将军因为兼管闽海关之故，是有名的肥缺，文煜一干十年，官囊极丰，有上百万的款子，存在阜康。汪惟贤知道胡雪岩跟他是在福州的旧识，交情甚厚，所以不嫌冒昧，借了他从福州带来的会做大菜——西餐的厨子，来接待福克与凯密伦。既然预备好了，自然是吃大菜。胡雪岩本有些话要问汪惟贤，但因他也是主人的身分，按西洋规矩，与汪惟贤分坐长餐桌的两端，不便交谈。直到饭罢，两洋客由阜康福中会说英语的伙计陪着去观光大栅栏以后，胡雪岩才能跟汪椎贤谈正事。
en: “Mr Hu,” Wang Weixian asked, “would you prefer Chinese food or Western food?” He promptly added a word about his own efforts. “I was afraid our two foreign guests might not take to Chinese dishes, so I specially borrowed a Western cook from His Excellency Wen. Everything is ready.” His Excellency Wen was Wenyu, the Minister of Punishments, a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner who had become Fuzhou Garrison General in the seventh year of Tongzhi. After the Qing forces entered the passes, garrison generals had been stationed at strategic points throughout the country. The Fuzhou post was famously lucrative because its holder also supervised the Fujian Maritime Customs. Wenyu had held it for ten years and accumulated a very substantial official purse; he had over a million deposited with Fukang. Wang knew that he and Hu were old friends from Fuzhou and on excellent terms. He had therefore felt free to borrow the cook Wenyu had brought from Fuzhou, who could prepare Western meals, to entertain Focke and Cameron. Since everything was ready, Western food it was. Hu had wanted to ask Wang several questions, but as they were both acting as hosts, Western custom placed them at opposite ends of the long dining table, making conversation difficult. Only after dinner, when English-speaking clerks from Fukangfu took the two foreigners to see Dashilan, could Hu discuss business with Wang.

zh: 正事中最要紧的一件，便是他此行的任务，跟左宗棠谈一笔三四百万两银子的借款。胡雪岩急于想知道的是，左宗棠人朝以后的境遇，“帘眷”是否仍如以前之隆，与两王——掌枢的恭亲王及光绪皇帝的生父醇亲玉的关系，以及在军机中的地位等等，必须了解得清清楚楚，他才能决定哪些话可以说，哪些事不必谈。“我看左大人在京里顿不长的。”汪惟贤也是杭州人，跟东家打乡谈，“待不长”称之为“顿不长”，使得胡雪岩大吃一惊。“为啥顿不长？”“还不是他的‘沃不烂，煮不熟’的老脾气又发作了。”“沃不烂、煮不熟”也是杭州的俚语，有刚愎自用之意。接着，汪惟贤举左宗棠在军机处议俄约及“海防”一事，来支持他的看法。
en: The most important matter was the purpose of Hu’s journey: to discuss with Zuo Zongtang a loan of three or four million taels of silver. Hu was eager to learn how Zuo had fared since entering the court. Did he still enjoy the same great favour from the empress dowagers behind the curtain? How did he stand with the two princes, Prince Gong, who headed the Grand Council, and Prince Chun, the Guangxu Emperor’s father? What position did he hold within the Council itself? Hu needed to understand all this thoroughly before deciding what he could say and what he had better leave unmentioned. “I don’t reckon His Excellency Zuo will stop long in the capital,” Wang said. Wang too was from Hangzhou and spoke to his employer in their native dialect, using its local word for “stay long”. The remark gave Hu a sharp shock. “Why won’t he stop long?” “His old temper has come out again: no amount of stewing will soften him, no amount of boiling will cook him.” This was another Hangzhou expression, meaning obstinately determined to have one’s own way. To support his opinion, Wang went on to describe Zuo’s conduct during Grand Council discussions of the Russian treaty and coastal defence.

zh: 原来新疆回民起义一起，俄国以保侨为名。出兵占领了伊犁，扬言暂时接管，回民起义一平，即当交还中国，及至左宗棠西征，先后克复乌鲁木齐、吐鲁番等重镇，天山南北路次第平靖，开始议及规夏伊犁、要求俄国实践诺言，而俄国推三阻四，久假不归的本意，逐渐暴露。于是左宗棠挟兵力以争，相持不下。这样到了光绪四年秋天，朝议决走循正式外交途径以求了结，特派左都御史崇厚为出使俄国饮差大臣，又赏内大臣衔，为与俄议约的全权大臣，许他便宜行事。这年腊月，崇厚取道法德两国，抵达俄京圣彼得堡，立即与俄国外务部尚书格尔思展开谈判。谈了半年才定议，而且崇厚以“便宜行事”的“全权大臣”资格，在黑海附近，签订了《里瓦几亚条约》，内容是割伊犁以西以南之地予俄，偿付“兵费”五百万卢布，增开通商口岸多处，许俄人通商西安、汉中、汉口，以及松花江至伯都呐贸易自由。
en: When the Muslim uprising had begun in Xinjiang, Russia had sent troops to occupy Ili under the pretext of protecting its subjects. It announced that the occupation was temporary and that Ili would be returned to China as soon as the uprising had been suppressed. In his western campaign, Zuo Zongtang had recovered such important towns as Urumqi and Turfan, restoring order in succession on both sides of the Tianshan Mountains. He then raised the question of recovering Ili and called on Russia to honour its promise. Russia made one excuse after another, gradually revealing its true intention: to keep what it had supposedly borrowed. Zuo brought military pressure to bear, but neither side would yield. In the autumn of the fourth year of Guangxu, the court decided to seek a settlement through formal diplomacy. Chonghou, the Left Censor-in-Chief, was appointed imperial envoy to Russia and given the honorary title of Minister of the Inner Court. As plenipotentiary for the treaty negotiations, he was authorized to act at his own discretion. In the last lunar month of that year, Chonghou travelled through France and Germany to St Petersburg and immediately began negotiations with Giers, the Russian foreign minister. After six months they reached an agreement. Exercising his discretionary powers as plenipotentiary, Chonghou signed the Treaty of Livadia near the Black Sea. It ceded the territory west and south of Ili to Russia, provided five million roubles in compensation for military expenses, opened several additional trading ports, and allowed Russian trade at Xi’an, Hanzhong and Hankou, as well as unrestricted trade along the Songhua River as far as Boduna.

zh: 消息传回国内，舆论大哗，痛责崇厚丧权辱国。而崇厚敢于订此条约，是因为背后有两个强有力的人在支持，一个是军机大臣沈桂芬，他是朝中足以与“北派”领袖李鸿藻抗衡的“南派”领袖，深得两宫太后的信任。一个是直隶总督北洋大臣李鸿章，以继承曾国藩的衣钵标榜，在军务与洋务两方面的势力，已根深柢固，难以摇撼。在议约的半年中，崇厚随时函商，获得沈、李二人的同意，才敢放心签约，而且未经请旨，即起程回国，留参赞邵友廉署理出使大臣。沈桂芬、李鸿章虽都赞成伊犁条约而动机不同。沈桂芬是因为僵持的局面持续，朝廷即不能不派重兵防守，左宗棠的洋债就不能不借，长此以往，浩繁的军费会搞得民穷财尽，用心可说是委曲求全。李鸿章就不同了，多少是有私心的，第一，如果中俄交恶而至于决裂，一旦开战，俄国出动海军，必攻天津，身为北洋大臣的李鸿章，就不知道拿什么抵挡了，其次，左宗棠不断借洋债扩充势力，自非李鸿章所乐见，伊犁事件一结束，左宗棠班师还朝，那就无异解甲归田了。
en: When the news reached China, public opinion erupted, denouncing Chonghou for surrendering sovereign rights and humiliating the country. He had dared sign the treaty because two powerful men stood behind him. One was Grand Councillor Shen Guifen, leader of the Southern faction at court, who could hold his own against Li Hongzao, leader of the Northern faction, and enjoyed the deep confidence of both empress dowagers. The other was Li Hongzhang, Governor-General of Zhili and Beiyang Minister, who presented himself as the heir to Zeng Guofan’s mantle. His influence in military and foreign affairs was firmly entrenched and difficult to shake. Throughout the six months of negotiations, Chonghou had regularly sought their advice by letter. Only after receiving Shen’s and Li’s approval had he felt safe in signing. He had then set off home without first requesting an imperial command, leaving his counsellor, Shao Youlian, to serve as acting envoy. Though Shen and Li both supported the Ili treaty, their motives differed. Shen believed that a continuing deadlock would oblige the court to maintain large forces on the frontier and Zuo to keep borrowing abroad. In time, the enormous military expenditure would impoverish the people and exhaust the treasury. His intention could be described as accepting a compromise to preserve the greater good. Li’s position was different and partly self-interested. First, if relations with Russia broke down and war followed, the Russian navy would surely attack Tianjin. As Beiyang Minister, he did not know what he could use to repel it. Second, Zuo’s continual foreign borrowing to extend his power was hardly something Li welcomed. Once the Ili affair was settled and Zuo brought his army home, it would be virtually the same as laying down his arms and retiring.

zh: 无奈崇厚的交涉办得实在不高明，两宫震怒，士林痛诋，连恭王与沈桂芬主持的总署——总理各国事务衙门行走的诸大臣，亦觉得过于委屈，有改议的必要。于是朝命以出使俄国大臣崇厚不候谕旨，擅自启程回国的罪名，开缺交部严加议处。所议的俄约，交六部九卿、翰詹科道妥议具奏。这就是明朝的所谓“延议”。廷议的结果，崇厚所签的条约，无一可许，两宫因而召开“御前会议”，慈禧太后原想严办崇厚，加以“翰林四谏”中的宝连与黄体芳，上奏力攻崇厚，而且语中侵及李鸿章与恭王，这一来，崇厚便免不了革职拿问，交刑部议罪， 虽非。 铛入狱， 而软禁在刑部提牢司的“火房”中，这度日如年的况味，也就可想而知了。
en: Unfortunately, Chonghou had conducted the negotiations so badly that both empress dowagers were furious and the scholarly world condemned him bitterly. Even the ministers serving in the Zongli Yamen, the office for foreign affairs headed by Prince Gong and Shen Guifen, thought the concessions excessive and considered revision necessary. The court accordingly removed Chonghou from his post as envoy to Russia for setting out home without awaiting an imperial order and referred him for severe disciplinary review. The Russian treaty was submitted to the Six Boards, the Nine Ministers, the Hanlin and Heir Apparent’s establishments, and the supervising secretaries and censors, for careful deliberation and a joint report. This was what the Ming dynasty had called a court deliberation. Its conclusion was that not a single provision of Chonghou’s treaty could be accepted. The two empress dowagers therefore convened an imperial conference. Cixi already intended to punish him severely; now Baolian and Huang Tifang, two of the Four Remonstrants of the Hanlin, submitted fierce attacks on him that also touched on Li Hongzhang and Prince Gong. Chonghou could no longer escape dismissal and arrest, followed by examination of his offences at the Ministry of Punishments. Though he was not thrown into prison in chains, he was confined in the heated room of the Ministry’s Prison Office. It was easy to imagine how each day there must have seemed a year.

zh: 此举是抵触“万国公法”的，各国公使，群起抗议，但朝廷不为所动，一面派使英兼使法的钦差大臣、曾国藩的长子曾纪泽兼使俄，谋求改约，一面将崇厚走了“斩监”的罪名。不过，朝廷亦并未放弃和平解决的意愿，备战以外，由李鸿章策动英、法、德三国公使，出面调停，免了崇厚的死刑，但仍监禁，然后曾纪泽才在光绪六年六月，由伦敦动身赴俄，修订崇约。交涉开始之时不会顺利，是可想而知的。幸而曾纪泽不愧名父之子，运用他对“万国公法”的知识、出使的经验及关系，促请英、法驻俄公使的协助，在左宗棠到京的前两天，与格尔思改走了约稿，伊犁收回，嘉峪通商，不明定可通至某处，松花江通航取消，只是赔偿“军费”增加四百万卢布，共为九百万。
en: This treatment conflicted with international law, and the foreign envoys protested as one, but the court remained unmoved. It appointed Zeng Jize, Zeng Guofan’s eldest son and currently imperial envoy to Britain and France, to serve concurrently as envoy to Russia and seek a revised treaty. At the same time, Chonghou was sentenced to beheading, to await review in prison. Yet the court had not abandoned hope of a peaceful settlement. Alongside its preparations for war, Li Hongzhang induced the British, French and German envoys to mediate. Chonghou’s death sentence was remitted, though he remained confined. Only then, in the sixth lunar month of the sixth year of Guangxu, did Zeng leave London for Russia to revise Chonghou’s treaty. The negotiations were bound to be difficult at first. Fortunately, Zeng proved worthy of his distinguished father. Drawing on his knowledge of international law, his diplomatic experience and his connections, he enlisted the help of the British and French envoys in Russia. Two days before Zuo Zongtang reached Beijing, he and Giers agreed on a revised draft: Ili would be recovered; trade through Jiayu Pass would be allowed without specifying how far inland it might extend; navigation on the Songhua River would be cancelled. The compensation for military expenses, however, was increased by four million roubles, making nine million in all.

zh: 当中俄关系紧张时，李鸿章提出“海防论”的主张，与左宗棠的“陆防论”针峰相对。及至左宗棠到京入军机，先议俄约，由于曾纪泽挽回利权之多，超过朝野的期望，左宗棠亦表示满意，无甚争执，后议李鸿章“海防”的计划，他的话就多了，由海防谈到陆防，一转而为西睡的形势，与他在新疆用兵的经过，滔滔不绝，目无余子，军机处只听得他一个人又说又笑，“礼绝百僚”的恭王，默坐一两个时辰，连句话都插不上。“大先生你想，”汪惟贤说：“不要说恭王，哪个都吃不消他。恭王忍了又忍，忍到后来，索性要军机章京把原折收了起来，不议了。”“不议了？”胡雪岩诧异：“李合肥的海防，规模大得很呢！要开办北洋舰队、电报局，多少人等着吃这块大肥肉，哪里就说说算数，不议了？”“喏，”汪惟贤放低了声音说：“毛病就出在这里，不议不可以，要议又怕我们左大人独讲空话。那就只有调虎离了山再议。”一听这话，胡雪岩心冷了一半。原以为有左宗棠这样一座靠山当大军机，将来要借洋债，必然由他来主持，财源滚滚不绝。如今看样子怕又要外放，自己的想法也就落空了。而且恭王似乎有些讨厌左宗棠，此事颇为不妙，只不知醇王待他如何？
en: During the tension with Russia, Li Hongzhang had advocated coastal defence in direct opposition to Zuo Zongtang’s emphasis on land defence. When Zuo arrived in Beijing and entered the Grand Council, the Russian treaty was discussed first. Zeng Jize had recovered more rights and interests than either the court or the public had expected, so Zuo too expressed satisfaction, and there was little dispute. But when discussion turned to Li’s coastal-defence plans, he had much more to say. From coastal defence he moved to land defence, then to conditions on the western frontier and the story of his campaigns in Xinjiang. He talked endlessly, as though nobody else mattered. In the Grand Council, only his voice and laughter could be heard. Prince Gong, whose rank placed him above all the officials, sat silently for two to four hours at a stretch without being able to get in a word. “Just think, Mr Hu,” Wang said. “Never mind Prince Gong; nobody could stand it. The prince endured it again and again, until at last he simply told the Council secretaries to put the original memorial away. They would discuss it no further.” “No further?” Hu was astonished. “Li of Hefei has enormous plans for coastal defence! There’s the Beiyang Fleet and the Telegraph Bureau to be set up. So many people are waiting for a bite of that rich meat. How can it all end with a few words and no more discussion?” “There,” Wang lowered his voice, “is the trouble. They have to discuss it, but if they do, they’re afraid our His Excellency Zuo will monopolize the conversation with empty talk. The only way is to lure the tiger away from the mountain before they resume.” Hu’s hopes sank halfway at these words. With a powerful patron like Zuo on the Grand Council, he had assumed that Zuo would inevitably take charge of future foreign loans, bringing an endless stream of profit. Now Zuo seemed likely to be sent out to a provincial post again, and Hu’s expectations would come to nothing. Worse still, Prince Gong appeared to dislike him. That did not bode well. But how did Prince Chun treat him?

zh: “醇王待他是好的。大先生晓得的，醇王是好武的一伙，左大人有这样的战功，拿他当个英雄看，所谓惺惺相惜，常常有往来，走得很近的，醇王还要请他到神机营去看操呢！”“你说啥！”胡雪岩问道：“醇王请左大人到神机营看操！”“是啊。”“你听哪个说的？”这话有不相信的意味，而且看得出来，胡雪岩很重视这件事，汪惟贤倒有些猜不透，只好据实作答。“我是听‘小军机’徐老爷说的。”汪惟贤又说：“左大人是正月底到京的，二月初醇亲王就请他吃饭，逛太平湖新修好的花园，二月十几又请，当面约他看操，左大人答应了，一定去，不过日子没有定。大先生这一来，大概要走日子了。”胡雪岩越发不解，不过他并未立即发问，先想了一下，何以醇亲王请左宗棠看操，先不能定日子，等他一来，才可以定日子呢？想通了才问：“你这话是听哪个说的，徐老爷？”“不是他还有哪个？”胡雪岩心想，“小军机徐老爷”——军机章京徐用仪，跟左宗棠的关系向来密切，左宗棠应酬京官，一直都托他经手，他要谈到左宗棠，话都是靠得住的。
en: “Prince Chun treats him well. You know he has a taste for military affairs, Mr Hu. With His Excellency Zuo’s military achievements, he regards him as a hero. As they say, men of spirit appreciate one another. They visit often and are very close. The prince has even invited him to watch the drills at Shenji Camp.” “What did you say?” Hu asked. “Prince Chun has invited His Excellency Zuo to watch the drills at Shenji Camp?” “Yes.” “Who told you that?” The question carried a note of disbelief. It was also clear that Hu considered the matter important. Unable to fathom his reaction, Wang could only answer truthfully. “Mr Xu, the ‘junior grand councillor’, told me. His Excellency Zuo arrived at the end of the first month. Early in the second, Prince Chun invited him to dinner and to see the newly completed garden at Taiping Lake. Sometime in the teens of that month, he invited him again and personally asked him to watch the drills. His Excellency Zuo promised that he would certainly come, but they didn’t fix a day. Now that you are here, Mr Hu, I expect they will.” Hu was more puzzled than ever, but he did not ask immediately. Why could no date be fixed for Prince Chun’s invitation until he himself arrived? Only when he had thought it through did he ask, “Who told you that? Mr Xu?” “Who else?” Mr Xu, the so-called junior grand councillor, was Xu Yongyi, a secretary of the Grand Council. Hu reflected that he had always been close to Zuo, who consistently entrusted him with arrangements for his dealings with officials in Beijing. Anything he said about Zuo could be relied upon.

zh: 继而转念，一客不烦二主，自己有好些事何不也委托了徐用仪？于是立刻关照杨帅爷写了个帖子，请徐用仪“小酌”，特别注明“盼即命驾，俾聆教益”，另外捡了四样杭州的名物，两只方裕和的火腿，十把舒莲记的檀香扇，四坛景阳观的酱菜，还有胡庆余堂的“本作货”辟瘟丹、虎骨本瓜烧之类，装了一网篮，伴着请帖，一起送到徐府。日落时分，徐用仪来了。还是穿了官服来的，他的底缺是刑部主事，胡雪岩的顶戴是珊瑚顶子，官阶差着一大截，所以用的是属员参见长官的礼节。“大人几时到京的？”徐用仪见了胡雪岩，急趋踱步，一面说话，一面捞起袍衬下摆，打算要请安了。徐用仪字筱云，胡雪岩跟他见过一次面，称他“筱翁”，这时急忙双手扶住，带着埋怨的语气说：“筱翁，筱翁，你这样子简直在骂人了。赶紧请换了衣服再说。”徐用仪的跟班，早就挟着衣包在廊上等候，听得这话，便进来伺候主人更换便衣。宝蓝宁绸夹袍，玫瑰紫贡缎琵琶襟坎肩，这是军机章京习惯成自然而专用的服饰，在应酬场中很出风头的。相互作了辑，上炕落坐，徐用仪改了称呼：“胡大先生是哪天到的？”
en: Then another thought struck Hu: why trouble two hosts when one would do? He too had many matters that could be entrusted to Xu. He immediately told Secretary Yang to write an invitation asking Xu to join him for a modest drink, with a special request that he come at once so Hu might benefit from his advice. He also selected four kinds of Hangzhou speciality: two Fang Yuhe hams, ten Shulianji sandalwood fans, four jars of Jingyangguan pickled vegetables, and Hu Qingyu Hall’s own products, including Biwen Pills and tiger-bone-and-papaya liquor. These were packed into a basket and sent with the invitation to Xu’s house. Xu arrived at sunset, still wearing his official robes. His substantive appointment was as a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, whereas Hu wore a coral button on his official hat. Their ranks were far apart, so Xu observed the formalities of a subordinate calling on a superior. “When did Your Excellency arrive in Beijing?” he asked, hurrying forward and gathering up the hem of his robe, ready to make his formal obeisance. Xu’s courtesy name was Xiaoyun. Hu, who had met him once before and addressed him as Mr Xiaoyun, quickly caught him with both hands. “Mr Xiaoyun, Mr Xiaoyun! You positively insult me with these formalities. Please change your clothes at once, and then we can talk.” Xu’s attendant was already waiting in the corridor with a bundle of clothes. At these words he came in to help his master change into informal dress: a lined gown of royal-blue Nanjing silk and a rose-purple tribute-satin vest with a curved, pipa-shaped front fastening. This had become the customary, distinctive attire of Grand Council secretaries and made quite a show in social gatherings. They exchanged bows and sat on the kang. Xu now changed his form of address. “On what day did you arrive, Mr Hu?”

zh: “刚到。我的第一位客，就是筱翁。”徐用仪有些受宠若惊似地，抱着拳文绘绘地说：“辱承不弃，又蒙宠赐多珍，真是既感且愧。”“小意思，小意思，何足道哉！”胡雪岩问：“筱翁跟左大人常见？”“天天见面的，该我的班，一天要见两回，早晨在军机处，下午在左大人的公馆贤良寺。”“他老人家精神倒还好？”“还好，还好。不过……”徐用仪微蹩着眉说：“好得有点过头了，反倒不大好。”“大概是他老人家话多之故？”“话不但多，中气还足。他在北屋高谈阔论，我们在南屋的人都听得到。”
en: “Just now. You are my first guest, Mr Xiaoyun.” Looking almost overwhelmed by the honour, Xu clasped his hands and replied in polished literary phrases. “Your gracious regard, and the many precious gifts you have so kindly bestowed, leave me at once grateful and ashamed.” “Mere trifles, mere trifles! Not worth mentioning.” Hu asked, “Do you see His Excellency Zuo often?” “Every day. When I’m on duty, twice a day: in the morning at the Grand Council, and in the afternoon at his residence in Xianliang Temple.” “Is the old gentleman keeping well?” “Very well, very well. Only…” Xu frowned slightly. “Rather too well, which is not altogether a good thing.” “Because he talks so much, I suppose?” “Not only does he talk a great deal; he has powerful lungs. When he holds forth in the north room, those of us in the south room can hear everything.”

zh: 胡雪岩点点头，暂且丢开左宗棠，“筱翁，”他说，“我在京里，两眼漆黑，全要靠你照应。”徐用仪知道这是客气话，胡雪岩拿银子当灯笼，双眼雪亮，当下答说：“不敢当，不敢当，如果有可以效劳的地方，不必客气，尽请吩咐。”“太言重了。”胡雪岩说：“我是真心要拜托筱翁，想请筱翁开个票子，哪里要应酬，哪里要自己去，应酬是怎么个应酬法？都请筱翁指点。还有个不情之请，这张票子，要请筱翁此刻就开。”这是委以重任了。徐用仪自然照办，想了一下说：“第一是同乡高官，尤其是言路上的几位，要多送一点。”“是的。请筱翁指示好了。说多少就是多少。”浅交而如此信任，徐用仪不免起了报答知己之感，“我要冒昧请教胡大先生，”他问：“这趟进京，是不是来谈借洋款的事？”“是的。”“还有呢？”“还有，想打听打听洋法缫丝，京里是怎么个宗旨？”“这容易，我就知道，回头细谈。”徐用仪接着又说：“如果是为借洋债的事，总理衙门的章京，户部的司官，不能不应酬。我开个单子出来。”于是端出笔砚，徐用仪就在茶几上开出一张单子，斟酌再三，在名字下写上数目，自一百至五百不等，自然是银票的数目。
en: Hu nodded and put Zuo aside for the moment. “Mr Xiaoyun, I am completely in the dark here in Beijing. I must depend on you to look after me.” Xu knew this was only courtesy. With silver for his lantern, Hu could see perfectly clearly. “You are too kind. If there is anything I can do, please give me your instructions without hesitation.” “You put it too strongly,” Hu said. “I truly do want to ask your help. Would you draw up a list for me? Whom must I attend to? Whom must I visit myself? And how should I go about it in each case? I should like your guidance on all these points. I have one further, unreasonable request: please draw up the list now.” This was an important responsibility, and Xu naturally agreed. After a moment’s thought he said, “First, the senior officials from your home province, especially those whose office is to remonstrate with the throne. They should receive rather more.” “Exactly. Please tell me what to do. Whatever amounts you say, I shall accept.” Such confidence from a man he scarcely knew made Xu feel that he must repay one who appreciated him. “May I venture to ask, Mr Hu, whether you have come to Beijing to discuss a foreign loan?” “Yes.” “Anything else?” “I also want to find out what view the capital takes of silk reeling by Western methods.” “That is easy. I know the answer myself; we can discuss it later. But if you are here about a foreign loan, the secretaries of the Zongli Yamen and the departmental officials of the Ministry of Revenue must receive attention. I’ll draw up a list.” Brush and inkstone were brought, and Xu wrote at the tea table. After careful consideration he put a figure beneath each name, ranging from one hundred to five hundred: the amounts, of course, to be given in banknotes.

zh: “有个人，怎么送法，要好好考究。”徐用仪搁笔说道：“为今管户部的是宝中堂，他又是总理大臣。”清朝有“大学士管部”的制度，勋业彪炳的左宗棠，以东阁大学士奉旨“人阁办事”。 自然是管兵部，宝鋆则是以武英殿大学士，继去世的文祥管户部，实掌度支大权。对于左宗棠借重息的洋债，啧有烦言，这是胡雪岩也知道的，为今听徐用仪提到宝鋆，正说到心事上，不由得便将身子凑了过去，声音也低了。“我没有跟宝中堂打过交道。请教筱翁，有没有路子？”“有条路子，我也是听说，不过可以试一试。”“什么路子？”“是这样的……”“法不传六耳”，徐用仪说得仅仅只有胡雪岩听得见。于是，在摆点心请徐用仪时，他抽个空将古应春找了来，有话交代。
en: “There is one man whose gift will require careful thought,” Xu said, laying down his brush. “Grand Secretary Bao now oversees the Ministry of Revenue, and he also serves in the Zongli Yamen.” Under the Qing system, grand secretaries were assigned oversight of ministries. Zuo Zongtang, with his outstanding military achievements, had been summoned to serve at court as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and naturally supervised the Ministry of War. Bao Yun, Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, had succeeded the late Wenxiang in supervising the Ministry of Revenue, giving him actual control over the national finances. He had often criticized Zuo’s high-interest foreign loans, as Hu was well aware. Xu’s mention of Bao touched the very point troubling him. He leaned closer and lowered his voice. “I have never had dealings with Grand Secretary Bao. Can you advise me, Mr Xiaoyun? Is there a way to approach him?” “There is one. I have only heard about it, but we could try.” “What is it?” “This is how it works…” A secret was not to be passed to a third pair of ears: Xu spoke so softly that only Hu could hear. Later, while refreshments were being served to Xu, Hu found an opportunity to call Gu Yingchun over and give him some instructions.

zh: “你对古董字玩都是内行，我想托你到琉璃厂走一趟。”古应春不免奇怪，胡雪岩到京，正事一件未办，倒忽然有闲情逸致要物色古董字画，其故安在？看出他心中的疑惑，胡雪岩便又说道：“我要买样东西送人。”原来是送礼，“送哪个？”古应春问。胡雪岩接过他的手来，在他掌心写了个“宝”字，然后开口：“明白？”“明白。”“好。”胡雪岩说：“琉璃厂有一家‘海岳山房’，上海的海，岳老爷的岳。你进去找一个姓朱的伙计，是绍兴人，你问他，某某人喜欢什么？他说字画，你就要字画，他说古董，你就要古董。并要关照：东西要好，价钱不论。”古应春将他的话细想了一遍，深深点头，表示会意：“我马上去。”等他回来，主客已经入席了。胡雪岩为古应春引见了徐用仪，然后说道：“来，来，陪筱翁多喝几杯？”接着又问：“怎么样？”“明天看东西。”
en: “You know antiques, calligraphy and paintings. I should like you to make a trip to Liulichang.” Gu was puzzled. Hu had only just arrived in Beijing and had not yet attended to a single item of business; why had he suddenly found the leisure to hunt for works of art? Seeing his doubt, Hu added, “I want to buy something as a gift.” So that was it. “For whom?” Gu asked. Hu took his hand and traced the character Bao on his palm. “Understand?” “I do.” “Good. There is a shop in Liulichang called Haiyue Shanfang: Hai as in Shanghai, Yue as in Lord Yue. Go in and ask for a clerk surnamed Zhu, a man from Shaoxing. Ask him what a certain person likes. If he says calligraphy and paintings, ask for those; if he says antiques, ask for antiques. And make it clear: the pieces must be good, whatever the price.” Gu considered these instructions carefully, then nodded emphatically to show that he understood. “I’ll go at once.” By the time he returned, host and guest were already at table. Hu introduced him to Xu. “Come, come, have a few more cups with Mr Xiaoyun.” Then he asked, “Well?” “I’m to see the goods tomorrow.”

zh: 胡雪岩知道搭上线上，便不再多问，转脸看着徐用仪说：“筱翁刚才说，如今做官有四条终南捷径，是哪四条？”“是四种身分的人：”帝师王佐，鬼使神差‘。象李兰荪、翁步平都是因为当皇上的师傅起家的，此谓之’帝师‘。宝中堂是恭王的死党，以前文中堂也是，这是’王佐‘。““文大人？”胡雪岩不觉诧异，“入阁拜相了。”徐用仪一愣，旋即省悟。他指的是已去世的体仁阁大学士文祥，胡雪岩却以为文煜升了协办大学士。当即答说：“尚书照例要转到吏部才会升协办，他现在是刑部尚书，还早。”“喔，喔，”胡雪岩也想到了，“筱翁是说以前的文文忠。”文忠是文祥的谥称。“不错。”“筱翁，”古应春插进来说：“ ‘鬼使’顾名思义，是出使外国，跟洋鬼子打交道。何谓‘神差’就费解了。”“一说破很容易明白。”徐用仪指着胡雪岩说：“刚才胡大先生跟我在谈神机营，‘神差’就是神机营的差使。因为醇王之故，在神机营当差，保举特优。不过汉人没分，就偶尔有，也是武将，文官没有在神机营当差的。”
en: Knowing that contact had been established, Hu asked no more. He turned to Xu. “You said just now that there are four shortcuts to official advancement these days, Mr Xiaoyun. What are they?” “Four sorts of people: imperial tutors, princely aides, envoys to devils, and men on divine commissions. Men like Li Lansun and Weng Buping made their way by teaching the emperor: those are the imperial tutors. Grand Secretary Bao is a devoted partisan of Prince Gong, as Grand Secretary Wen used to be. Those are the princely aides.” “His Excellency Wen?” Hu exclaimed. “Has he become a grand secretary?” Xu paused in surprise, then understood. He meant the late Wenxiang, Grand Secretary of the Tiren Pavilion, whereas Hu thought Wenyu had been promoted to assistant grand secretary. “As a rule, a minister has to be transferred to the Ministry of Personnel before he can become assistant grand secretary. He is still Minister of Punishments. It will be some time yet.” “Ah, yes,” Hu said, understanding in turn. “You mean the late Wen Wenzhong.” Wenzhong was Wenxiang’s posthumous name. “Exactly.” “Mr Xiaoyun,” Gu put in, “‘envoys to devils’ explains itself: men sent abroad to deal with foreign devils. But what are these ‘divine commissions’?” “Once explained, it is quite simple.” Xu gestured towards Hu. “Mr Hu and I were just discussing Shenji Camp; shen in its name means divine. A ‘divine commission’ means a posting there. Because of Prince Chun, men serving in the camp receive exceptionally favourable recommendations for promotion. But Han Chinese have no share in it. Even the occasional exception is a military officer. There are no Han civil officials serving there.”

zh: “应春，”胡雪岩说：“刚刚我跟筱翁在谈，醇王要请左大人到神机营去看操，左大人要等我来定日子，你道为啥？为的是去看操要犒赏，左大人要等我来替他预备。你倒弄个章程出来。古应春心想，犒赏兵丁，无非现在有阜康福钱庄在此，左宗棠要支银，派人来说一声就是。不此之图，自然是认为犒赏现银不适宜，要另想别法。“我们也不晓得人家喜欢什么东西？”古应春建议，“我看不如索性请荣大人到醇王那里去老实问一问，该怎么犒赏，听醇王的吩咐预备。”“荣仲华早已不上醇王的门了。”荣仲华就是荣禄，大家都知道他是醇王一手所提拔，居然不上“举主”的门了，宁非怪事？这就连胡雪岩也好奇地要一问究竟。“说来话长。其中还牵涉到一桩谈起来任何人都不会相信的秘密。”徐用仪放低声音问道：“你们在南边有没有听说过，西太后是什么病？”“听说是干血痨。”胡雪岩答说：“怎么会弄出来这个毛病？”“是……”徐用仪突然顿住，“这话以不说为宜，两位亦以不听为妙，听了不小心传出去会闯大祸，那就是我害了两位了。我们谈别的吧。”说到紧要之处，徐用仪忽然卖起关子来，胡雪岩不免怏怏。但转念觉得徐用仪如此谨慎小心，倒是可信任的。这一转念间，心中的不怏，涣然而释。
en: “Yingchun,” Hu said, “Mr Xiaoyun and I were just talking about Prince Chun’s invitation to His Excellency Zuo to watch the drills at Shenji Camp. His Excellency is waiting for me to arrive before fixing the day. Do you know why? Because he must reward the troops when he goes, and he is waiting for me to prepare the rewards. Work out a plan for me.” Gu reflected that rewarding troops ordinarily meant paying cash. With Fukangfu Bank here, Zuo need only send someone over to say that he wanted silver. Since he had not done so, he must consider cash unsuitable and want something else. “We don’t know what they would like,” Gu suggested. “Why not simply ask His Excellency Rong to go to Prince Chun and inquire frankly? We can prepare the rewards according to the prince’s instructions.” “Rong Zhonghua stopped calling at Prince Chun’s house long ago,” Xu said. Rong Zhonghua was Ronglu, whom everyone knew to have been raised to prominence by the prince himself. That he should no longer visit his own patron was extraordinary. Even Hu wanted to know why. “It is a long story, involving a secret that nobody would believe.” Xu lowered his voice. “Have you heard in the south what illness the Western Empress Dowager is suffering from?” “I heard it was dry-blood wasting disease,” Hu replied. “How could she have developed such an illness?” “It is…” Xu broke off abruptly. “Better that I should not speak of it, and better that you should not hear it. If you heard and accidentally passed it on, it could bring terrible trouble. I should have harmed you both. Let us talk of something else.” Hu was disappointed to have Xu become mysterious just at the critical point. Then he reflected that such caution made Xu a man to be trusted, and his disappointment dissolved.

zh: 于是又把杯闲谈了片刻，徐用仪因为初次同席，不肯多饮，要了一碗粥喝完，预备告辞了。“惟贤！”胡雪岩问道：“预备好了没有？”“预备好了。”汪惟贤亲自端来一个托盘，上有十几个红封套，另外一张名单，这是要托徐用仪代为致送的“菲敬”。“拜托，拜托！”胡雪岩拱拱手说：“其余的我亦照筱翁的意思办，或我亲自去拜候，或我派人送，尽明天一天办妥。”“好！好！”徐用仪问：“胡大先生你明天什么时候去看左大人？”“一早去等他。”“那么明天我们在贤良寺见，有话到时候再说。”“是，是！”胡雪岩一面说，一面向汪惟贤手一伸，接过来一个红封套，抽出里面的银票来看，照他的意思，开出四百两不误，便悄悄塞到徐用仪手中，顺势捏住，不让他推辞。“不，不！没有这个道理。”“小意思。筱翁不收就是不拿我胡某人做朋友。”“真是受之有愧。谢谢，谢谢。”
en: They drank and chatted a little longer. Since this was his first time at Hu’s table, Xu would not drink much. He asked for a bowl of rice gruel, finished it and prepared to leave. “Weixian,” Hu called, “is everything ready?” “It is.” Wang himself brought a tray containing more than ten red envelopes and a list of names. These were the “small tokens of respect” Xu was to deliver on Hu’s behalf. “I am most obliged,” Hu said, clasping his hands. “I shall deal with the others just as you advised, either calling myself or sending someone with the gift. Everything will be done tomorrow.” “Good, good. When will you see His Excellency Zuo tomorrow, Mr Hu?” “I shall go early and wait for him.” “Then we will meet at Xianliang Temple and talk further there.” “Yes, indeed.” As he spoke, Hu held out a hand to Wang, took a red envelope, and drew out the banknote to check it. It had been made out for four hundred taels, exactly as he had instructed. He quietly slipped it into Xu’s hand and closed his own hand over it so that Xu could not refuse. “No, no! There is no reason for this.” “A mere trifle. If you will not accept it, you do not regard me as a friend.” “I truly feel ashamed to accept it. Thank you, thank you.”

zh: 等客人走了，胡雪岩问起海岳山房的情形，古应春告诉他说，会到了姓朱的伙计，问起宝鋆喜欢什么，姓朱的答说都喜欢。古应春便照胡雪岩的话交代，价钱贵不要紧，只要东西好，当下约走次日上午看货。“你早点去。看过了，马上陪洋人到紧良寺来。”胡雪岩又说：“左大人犒赏神机营，我倒想好了一个办法，不知道办得通，办不通，都等明天下午再谈吧！”说罢，打了一个呵欠。海岳山房的朱伙计，外号“朱铁口”，所以有这个仿佛星相术上艺名的外号的由来是，他对古董、字画、版本的鉴别，无一不精，视其必真，说伪必伪。因此，虽是受人雇用的伙计，而琉璃厂中古玩铺、南海店的掌柜，当面都尊称他为“朱先生”。古应春做事很精细，知道了朱铁口的本事，有意拉交情，委屈自己主顾的身分，也称他为“朱先生”，朱铁口自然谦称“万不敢当”，自己建议：“叫我老朱好了。”“恭敬不如从命。”古应春说道：“老朱，你有些什么东西给我看。”那一声“朱先生”改变了朱铁口平时接待顾客的方式，“东西很多。”他随手捧起一方砚池说：“古老爷，你看。”
en: After Xu had left, Hu asked about Haiyue Shanfang. Gu said that he had met the clerk surnamed Zhu and asked what Bao Yun liked. Zhu had replied that he liked everything. Gu had then repeated Hu’s instructions: a high price did not matter, provided the pieces were good. They had arranged for him to inspect the goods the following morning. “Go early. As soon as you have seen them, bring the foreigners to Xianliang Temple,” Hu said. “As for His Excellency Zuo’s rewards for Shenji Camp, I have thought of a plan myself. Whether it can be carried out or not, we will leave that until tomorrow afternoon.” He yawned. The clerk at Haiyue Shanfang was nicknamed Zhu Tiekou, or Iron Mouth Zhu, a name that sounded like a fortune-teller’s professional title. He had earned it through his unfailing judgment of antiques, paintings, calligraphy and book editions: what he declared genuine was genuine; what he called false was false. Although only an employee, he was respectfully addressed as Mr Zhu by the proprietors of Liulichang’s antique shops and Nanhai shops. Gu, always careful in his dealings, had learned of his abilities and wanted to cultivate his friendship. Putting aside the superior standing of a customer, he too called him Mr Zhu. Zhu naturally protested that he did not deserve such respect and suggested, “Just call me Old Zhu.” “Better to obey than insist on courtesy,” Gu replied. “Old Zhu, what have you to show me?” That single “Mr Zhu” had altered Zhu’s usual manner of receiving customers. “A great many things.” He picked up an inkstone. “Look at this, Mr Gu.”

zh: 古应春看即方砚池七寸长、五寸宽、三寸高，色如猪肝，正面两边各有一行篆字，右边是“丹心贯日”，左边是“汤阴鹏举志”。“原来是岳武穆用过的。”“不光是岳武穆用过，明太祖还用过呢！”朱铁口微笑着说。古应春仔细一看，砚池右侧还刻着四行楷书：“岳少保砚向供宸御，今蒙上赐臣达。古忠臣宝砚也，臣何能堪？谨矢竭忠贞，无辱此砚。洪武二年正月朔日，臣徐达谨记。”“ 徐达是明朝开国元勋第一位，又是明太祖的儿女亲家，这方砚有这样的来历，明朝人的笔记当中，一定有记载的。老朱，你说是不是？”朱铁口笑了，“听古老爷这话，就晓得是内行。真人面前不说假话，是不是中山王徐达收藏过，也不必去谈它了。”他将砚池置回原处又说：“古老爷，你请里面来坐。”
en: The inkstone was seven cun long, five wide and three high, and the colour of pig’s liver. A line of seal-script characters ran down either side of its upper surface. On the right was “A loyal heart shines through the sun”; on the left, “Inscribed by Pengju of Tangyin.” “So it was used by Yue Fei, Lord Wumu.” “Not only by Lord Wumu. The founding emperor of the Ming used it too,” Zhu said with a smile. Looking more closely, Gu saw four lines in regular script carved on the right side: “The inkstone of Yue, the Junior Guardian, formerly served the imperial presence. His Majesty has now graciously bestowed it upon his servant Da. It is the precious inkstone of a loyal minister of old. How can I be worthy of it? I solemnly pledge my utmost loyalty and devotion, that I may bring no dishonour upon this inkstone. Respectfully recorded by the servant Xu Da on the first day of the first month in the second year of Hongwu.” “Xu Da ranked first among the founders of the Ming, and his children married into the founding emperor’s family,” Gu said. “With such a history, this inkstone must surely appear in some Ming scholar’s collected notes. Wouldn’t you say so, Old Zhu?” Zhu laughed. “One can tell from that remark that you know your subject, Mr Gu. No false words before a true master. Whether Xu Da, Prince of Zhongshan, ever owned it is something we needn’t discuss.” He put the inkstone back. “Please come inside and sit down.”

zh: 所谓“里面”是帐柜后面的一间斗室，一关上门，就靠屋顶一方天窗透光进来，阳光斜射，恰好照亮靠壁的方桌。朱铁口等古应春在对面坐定，方始俯身向前，低声开口，神态显得神秘而郑重。“古老爷，你是哪位介绍你来的？”“是我的东家交代我来的，没有人介绍。”“贵东家是哪位？”古应春有些踌躇，不知道能不能透露胡雪岩的姓名，因而久久未答。“古老爷，”朱铁口说：“贵东家是怎么关照你的？”“就说让我来找你老朱，问一问宝中堂喜欢什么。东西要好。价钱不在乎。”“那就怪不得你不肯说破了，贵东家没有交代清楚。”朱铁口说：“贵东家要买古董字画送宝中堂，当然是有作用的。到底是为了啥，预备送值多少钱的东西？古老爷，你老实告诉我，我来替你盘算一下，包你一钱不落虚空地，都用在刀口上。”古应春听出话中大有曲折，看朱铁口意思诚恳，便老实答道：“确如你所说，敝东家没有交代清楚。老朱，你能不能先把其中的奥妙告诉我，我再看能不能替敝东家作主。”“这有何不可。”朱铁口说：“我们这里跟各王府，几位中堂府上都有往来的，说穿了……”
en: “Inside” meant a tiny room behind the accounts counter. Once the door was shut, its only light came through a skylight in the roof. A slanting ray of sunshine fell neatly across the square table against the wall. When Gu had seated himself opposite, Zhu leaned forward and spoke in a low voice, his manner solemn and mysterious. “Who introduced you to us, Mr Gu?” “My employer told me to come. There was no introduction.” “And who is your employer?” Gu hesitated, uncertain whether he could reveal Hu’s name, and did not answer for some time. “What instructions did your employer give you, Mr Gu?” “Only to find you, Old Zhu, and ask what Grand Secretary Bao likes. The pieces must be good; the price doesn’t matter.” “Then it’s no wonder you won’t tell me everything. Your employer didn’t make himself clear. Naturally, he has some purpose in buying antiques and paintings for Grand Secretary Bao. What exactly is it? How much does he intend to give? Tell me frankly and I’ll work it out for you. I guarantee that not a penny will be wasted; every bit will go where it counts.” Gu could hear that there was much beneath these words. Zhu seemed sincere, so he answered honestly. “You are quite right. My employer did not explain clearly. Could you first tell me how it all works, Old Zhu? Then I can judge whether I may act on his behalf.” “Of course. We have dealings with the various princely households and several grand secretaries’ residences. To put it plainly…”

zh: 说穿了是卖官鬻爵，过付之处，公然受贿，有所不便，所以要有人居间来遮蔽形迹。“假使说，你古老爷想放个考官，或者少爷乡试要下场了。怕‘场中莫论文’，想买个‘关节’，就得要到打磨厂去请教江西金谿人开的卖‘闱墨’的书坊，他们会跟你讲价钱。倘或要谋缺谋差呢，就得来找我们，我们会替你去问了来告诉你，要送什么东西，自然是在我们这里买……”“慢慢！”古应春打断他的话问：“你是说一定要在你这里买？”“是的。”“价钱由你开？”“当然。”“能不能还价？”“能还价，怎么不能？”朱铁口说，“古老爷承你看得起，我不忍赚你的昧心钱，所以要请你告诉我，贵东家打算谋个什么差缺，我好告诉你真正的行情。““嗯，嗯。”古应春细想了一下，还有不甚明白的地方，便义说道：“请你打个比方我听听。”
en: To put it plainly, this was the sale of offices and honours. It was inconvenient for those receiving the payments to take bribes openly, so intermediaries were needed to conceal the transaction. “Suppose you wanted an appointment as an examiner, Mr Gu, or your son was about to sit the provincial examination. Afraid that literary merit might count for nothing in the examination hall, you might want to buy a private arrangement. Then you would go to Damochang, to the shops selling collections of examination essays, run by men from Jinxi in Jiangxi. They would quote you a price. But if you wanted a post or a commission, you would come to us. We would make inquiries and tell you what you must give. Naturally, you would buy it here…” “Wait,” Gu interrupted. “Do you mean it has to be bought from you?” “Yes.” “At a price you set?” “Of course.” “Can one bargain?” “Certainly. Why not? You have been good enough to think well of me, Mr Gu, and I couldn’t bear to make a dishonest profit from you. That is why I ask what post your employer wants, so that I can tell you the true going rate.” “I see.” Gu thought it over, but some points were still unclear. “Give me an example.”

zh: “比方，你老想放上海道。我去问了来告诉你，送宝中堂一部《玉枕兰亭》就可以了。这部帖要十二万银子，你买了这部帖送进去，宝中堂知道已经到手了，就会如你所愿。其实呢，上海道的行情是十万银子，我们外加两成帽子，内扣两成回佣，一笔交易赚四万。如果主顾精明，磨来磨去讨价还价，顶多磨掉外加的那两成帽子，至于放交情，象你老这样的，我就老实告诉你。十万银子一文不能少。”“喔，原来如此。”古应春又问：“如果不知道你们这里这条门路，另外托人去活动呢？”“他们也会告诉你，送一部《玉枕兰亭》，而且告诉你要到哪里去买。”朱铁口又说：“这个法子是乾隆年间和坤发明的，他说送什么东西，根本就是他自己的收藏，我们去问价钱的时候，顺便就把东西带回来了。”
en: “Suppose you wanted to be Shanghai Circuit Intendant. I would inquire and tell you that all you needed was to give Grand Secretary Bao a copy of the Jade-Pillow Lanting calligraphy album. The album would cost a hundred and twenty thousand taels. You would buy it and send it in. Once the grand secretary knew the money was in hand, you would get your wish. The actual price of the Shanghai post is a hundred thousand. We add twenty per cent on top and deduct twenty per cent as commission, making forty thousand on the transaction. A shrewd customer who haggles and haggles can at most knock off the twenty per cent added on top. For someone to whom I want to show friendship, such as yourself, I would state it frankly: a hundred thousand, and not a single coin less.” “Ah, so that is how it works. What if someone didn’t know this route through your shop and approached someone else to arrange it?” “They too would tell him to give a copy of the Jade-Pillow Lanting, and tell him where to buy it.” Zhu continued, “Heshen invented this method in the Qianlong reign. Whatever item he told a man to give was actually from his own collection. When we went to ask the price, we simply brought the object back with us.”

zh: “多谢，多谢！我学到了一个秘诀。不过，还有一点想请教，譬如说，我倒不想计价还价，直接想送某人多少，这又该怎么办呢？”“这我们也有规矩的。先问你送什么人，送恭王有送恭王的东西，送宝中堂有送宝中堂的东西。譬如你说送恭王，我会告诉你，喏，这方岳少保砚，两千，那部‘阁帖’三千，一部宋版杜诗五千，你如果想送一万银子，凑起来正好。”“有没有帽子在里头？”“货真价实，不加帽子。”朱铁口解释这种情形跟卖差卖缺不同，譬如上海道一缺值十万银子，收到十万，则该到手都到手了，外加帽子吃亏的是“买主”。倘或有人想送八万，而实际上照底价只是七万银子的东西，岂不是侵吞了“卖主”应得之款？信用一失，另觅别家过付，这样好的买卖做不成，真正贪小失大，不智之甚。
en: “Thank you, thank you. I have learned a secret. But there is one more point. Suppose I didn’t want to bargain at all, but simply wanted to give someone a certain sum. How would that be done?” “We have rules for that too. First we ask whom you want to give it to. There are things for Prince Gong and things for Grand Secretary Bao. Say you wanted to give something to Prince Gong. I would tell you: this inkstone of Yue, the Junior Guardian, is two thousand; that Ge Tie calligraphy album is three thousand; a Song edition of Du Fu’s poems is five thousand. If you wanted to give ten thousand taels, they would add up exactly.” “Would there be a markup in those prices?” “Genuine goods at fair prices. No markup.” Zhu explained that this differed from selling posts and appointments. If the Shanghai post was worth a hundred thousand taels, then once that amount was received, all that was due had been paid. Any additional markup came at the buyer’s expense. But if a man intended to give eighty thousand and the goods were actually worth only seventy thousand at the agreed base prices, would that not be taking money owed to the seller? Once trust was lost, the seller would use another intermediary. To lose such excellent business for a small immediate gain would be exceedingly foolish.

zh: “老朱，你把话都说明了。我也不能有一点骗你。敝东家不是谋差谋缺，另有缘故，想送多少我虽还不知道，不过猜想不是三、五万银子的事。等找回去间清楚了，我们再进一步商量。”古应春又加重了语气说，“老朱，你请放心。除非不送，要送一定请你经手，即使敝东家想另找别家，我也不会答应的。”看他说得如此诚恳，又看他的仪表服饰，朱铁口知道遇见阔客了，这件事成功，掌柜起码要分他几千银子，大可自立门户了。转念到此，心花怒放，“古老爷载培，感激不尽。”朱铁口站起身来请了个安说：“古老爷想来收藏很多，不知道喜欢玩点什么，看看我能不能效劳？”古应春心想，即然拉交情，即不能空手而回，但一时想不起要些什么，便信口问道：“有没有什么新奇的东西？”“有，怎么没有。古老爷请到外面来看。”
en: “Old Zhu, since you have told me everything, I must not deceive you in the least. My employer is not seeking a post or an appointment; he has another purpose. I don’t yet know how much he intends to give, but I suspect this is no mere matter of thirty or fifty thousand taels. Let me go back and ask him clearly, and then we can discuss it further.” Gu added with emphasis, “Rest assured: unless he decides to give nothing, the transaction will certainly go through you. Even if my employer wanted to use another shop, I wouldn’t agree.” Hearing his sincerity and observing his appearance and dress, Zhu knew he had found a wealthy customer. If the business succeeded, the proprietor would have to give him at least several thousand taels. He could easily set up for himself. The thought delighted him. “I cannot thank you enough for your patronage, Mr Gu.” He rose and made an obeisance. “You must have a considerable collection yourself. What do you like? Let me see whether I can be of service.” Gu thought that if he wanted to make a friend, he ought not to leave empty-handed. Unable to think immediately of anything he wanted, he asked casually, “Have you anything unusual?” “Indeed I have. Please come out and look.”

zh: 朱铁口寻寻觅觅，找出来四样古玩，长圆方扁不一，长的是仿佛黄玉所制的萧，圆的是一具大明宣德年制的蟋蟀罐，方的是明朝开国元勋魏国公徐辉祖蒙御赐得以免死的铁券，扁的是康熙年所制的“葫芦器”，是一只印泥盒。“古老爷，你倒估估看，哪一样最值钱？”“应该是这一支玉萧。”“玉萧？你老倒仔细看一看，是不是玉？”古应春拿起那支萧，用手指弹了两下，其声铿然，“不是玉是什么？”他问。“你再看。”再看上面有题词：“外不泽，中不干，受气独全，其音不窒不浮，品在佳竹以上。”字是墨迹。玉器何能着墨？这就奇怪了。“是纸萧，出在福建。”朱铁口说：“这是明朝的东西，制法现在已经失传。”
en: After some searching, Zhu produced four curios, respectively long, round, square and flat. The long object was a xiao flute that appeared to be made of yellow jade. The round one was a cricket jar from the Xuande reign of the Ming. The square one was an iron certificate of immunity from execution, bestowed by the emperor on Xu Huizu, Duke of Wei, a founding worthy of the Ming. The flat one was a moulded-gourd object from the Kangxi reign: a box for seal paste. “Which would you say is worth most, Mr Gu?” “I should think this jade flute.” “Jade? Look carefully. Is it jade?” Gu picked up the flute and tapped it twice with a finger. It rang clearly. “What is it, if not jade?” “Look again.” On closer inspection he found an inscription: “Not lustrous without, not dry within; it receives the breath whole. Its tone is neither stifled nor floating, and its quality surpasses the finest bamboo.” The writing was in ink. How could ink adhere to jade? That was strange. “It is a paper flute, made in Fujian,” Zhu said. “It dates from the Ming. The method of making it has now been lost.”

zh: 古应春大为惊异，随手摆在一旁，表示中意要买，然后问道：“老朱，你说哪样东西最难得？”物以稀为贵，最难得的自然值钱，朱铁口小心翼翼地拿起那具蟋蟀罐，用指轻扣，渊渊作金石之声，很满意地说道：“不假，五百年前的东西。”见此光景，古应春好奇心起，接过那具陶罐细看，罐子四周雕镂人物，罐底正中刻着“大明宣德年制”，另有一行小字：“苏州陆墓邹大秀敬造”。但制作虽相当精巧，毕竟只是个蟋蟀罐，经历四五百年，也不能就算值钱的古董。他不好意思直抒观感，只好这样问说：“老朱，你说它好处在哪里？”“好处在旧、在有土性，火气尽脱，才不伤虫。古老爷，你总斗过蛐蛐吧？”蟋蟀在北方唤做“蛐蛐”，南方亦有此称呼，古应春虽不好此道，但斗蟋蟀搏彩，输赢进出极大，他是知道的。“一场蛐蛐下来，银子上千上万算，好蛐蛐说得难听些，真当它祖宗看待，上百两银子一只宣德盆，又算得了啥？”古应春暗暗咋舌，“一只瓦罐，值一百两银子？”他问。“是的。不过古老爷要，当然特别克己。”朱铁口说：“四样东西，一共算二百两银子好了。”
en: Greatly surprised, Gu set the flute aside to show that he liked it and would buy it. “Which is the rarest piece, Old Zhu?” Rarity made for value, so the rarest should naturally be the most expensive. Zhu carefully lifted the cricket jar and tapped it with a finger. It gave a deep, resonant ring like metal or stone. “Genuine. Five hundred years old,” he said with satisfaction. His manner aroused Gu’s curiosity. Taking the earthenware jar, Gu examined it closely. Figures were carved around its sides. In the centre of the base were the words “Made in the Xuande Reign of the Great Ming,” with a smaller line beside them: “Respectfully made by Zou Daxiu of Lumu, Suzhou.” The workmanship was certainly delicate, but it was only a cricket jar. Having survived four or five hundred years did not in itself make it a valuable antique. Gu felt awkward about saying so directly. “What is so good about it, Old Zhu?” “Its age, and the quality of its clay. All the fierceness of the firing has left it, so it won’t harm the insect. You have fought crickets, surely?” Crickets were called ququ in the north, and sometimes in the south as well. Though Gu did not pursue the pastime, he knew that enormous sums changed hands in wagers on cricket fights. “A single contest can involve thousands or tens of thousands of taels. To put it bluntly, they treat a good cricket like an honoured ancestor. What is a hundred-odd taels for a Xuande jar to such a man?” Gu marvelled inwardly. “A hundred taels for an earthenware pot?” “Yes. But for you, of course, I would make a special concession. Let us say two hundred taels for all four pieces.”

zh: 这不应该算贵，古应春一语不发，从身上掏出来一个洋式的皮夹，取出来一叠银票，凑好数目二百两，收起皮夹。朱铁口在一旁看得很清楚，所有的银票都是阜康福所出，当下灵机一动，惊喜地说道：“原来古老爷的贵东家，就是‘胡财神’。胡雪岩被称为“胡财神”，已有好几年了。古应春不便否认，只低声说道：“老朱，你知道就好。放在肚子里！一张扬开来，这笔交易就做不成了。”“我知道，我知道，这种事怎么好张扬？”古应春点点头，关照老朱将四样古玩送到阜康福，自己坐着车匆匆进城，赶到冰盏胡同贤良寺去作翻译。
en: That could hardly be considered expensive. Without a word, Gu took a Western-style leather wallet from his clothes, drew out a sheaf of banknotes, counted out two hundred taels and put the wallet away. Watching closely, Zhu saw that every note had been issued by Fukangfu. A sudden realization made him exclaim in delighted surprise, “So your employer is Hu, the God of Wealth!” Hu had been known by that name for several years. Gu could hardly deny it. He merely lowered his voice. “It is enough that you know, Old Zhu. Keep it to yourself. If the news gets about, this transaction will be impossible.” “I understand, I understand. How could anyone spread word of such a thing?” Gu nodded and told Zhu to deliver the four curios to Fukangfu. He himself hurried into the city by carriage, making for Xianliang Temple in Bingzhan Hutong to act as interpreter.
